### Interpretation


| Variable | Negative Cor | Positive Cor | Interpretation |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `prop_swf` | Correlates negatively with `l_contag` (-0.41), clay (-0.21), `fert_N` (-0.19), `treeage` (-0.18), `AFage` (-0.26), and area (-0.34). | Slightly positive correlation with mean slope (0.20), min slope (0.27), and `prop_swf_within` (0.36). | `CONTAG` is an aggregation metric based on cell adjacencies and describes the probability that two randomly selected cells belong to the same class. More small woody features may reduce landscape aggregation because they introduce small patches that disrupt the landscape. Clay: no interpretation. Slope: no clear interpretation. Field design: no clear interpretation. |
| `l_contag` | Correlates negatively with min slope (-0.54), mean slope (-0.49), `prop_swf` (-0.41), `l_shdi` (-0.39), `l_sidi` (-0.53), `l_ed` (-0.34), `prop_swf_within` (-0.22), sand (-0.20), and precipitation (-0.19). | Strongly positively correlated with area (0.74), `treeage` (0.52), `AFage` (0.50), `l_ai` (0.34), and clay (0.32). | Landscape metrics were calculated within a 3000 m buffer including the field. Large fields may create larger class areas, increasing the contagion index. The negative correlation with Shannon and Simpson diversity is expected because these metrics capture different aspects of landscape structure. |
| `l_np` | Correlates negatively with `l_ai` (-0.75), `temp_C_mean` (-0.56), solar radiation (-0.37), sand (-0.36), max slope (-0.31), `fert_N` (-0.30), and `treeage` (-0.29). | Positively correlated with `l_shdi`, `l_ed` (0.76), precipitation (0.49), clay (0.39), silt (0.32), mean slope (0.32), and min slope (0.45). | Number of patches within the 3000 m buffer. Wetter, cooler, and flatter fields tend to have more land-cover patches. |
| `l_shdi` | Correlates negatively with `prop_swf_within` (-0.59), `treeage` (-0.46), `l_ai` (-0.41), area (-0.41), `l_contag` (-0.39), `temp_C_mean` (-0.29), sand (-0.28), and `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (-0.21). | Positively correlated with mean slope (0.65), min slope (0.58), `l_ed` (0.45), max slope (0.43), clay (0.32), precipitation (0.31), and silt (0.22). | Shannon diversity index, describing how many land-cover classes are present and how evenly they are distributed. Steeper fields correlate with more diverse landscapes. The negative correlation with `prop_swf_within` may indicate that a high proportion of SWF causes one land-cover class to dominate, thereby reducing Shannon diversity. Treeage: no clear interpretation. Climate and soil correlations: no clear interpretation. |
| `l_sidi` | NA | NA | Very similar in values and identical in direction to `l_shdi`; better to choose one of the two. |
| `l_ed` | Correlates almost perfectly negatively with `l_ai` (-1.00), and negatively with area (-0.65), `temp_C_mean` (-0.62), `treeage` (-0.62), `fert_N` (-0.46), `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (-0.43), sand (-0.41), `l_contag` (-0.34), max slope (-0.32), and `AFage` (-0.23). | Strongly positively correlated with min slope (0.85), mean slope (0.68), precipitation (0.65), `l_shdi` (0.45), clay (0.43), `prop_swf_within` (0.36), and silt (0.33). | `ED` is an area/edge metric measuring total edge length between patches per unit area. Its perfect negative correlation with `l_ai` suggests that one of these metrics may need to be dropped. Steeper fields occur in landscapes with more edge, consistent with the `l_shdi`–slope relationship. Wetter/cooler climates also show more edge, although this may reflect a regional confound between climate and field location. Fertilization, soil texture, and field-design correlations: no clear interpretation. |
| `l_ai` | NA | NA | Contains essentially the same information as `l_ed` but with reversed sign; better to choose one of the two. |
| `distance_to_tree_strip` | No notable negative correlations. | Slight positive correlation with `AFage` (0.22). | Essentially uncorrelated with the other field-level landscape and environmental variables, which is a good sign because it does not appear strongly confounded with these predictors. |
| `temp_C_mean` | Strongly negatively correlated with precipitation (-0.77), `l_ed` (-0.62), min slope (-0.48), clay (-0.46), mean slope (-0.44), silt (-0.39), `l_shdi` (-0.29), and `prop_swf_within` (-0.18). | Strongly positively correlated with `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (0.82), `l_ai` (0.61), sand (0.45), area (0.23), and `treeage` (0.22). | Warmer fields are generally sunnier and drier. Warmer sites also tend to be flatter, sandier, and located in more aggregated landscapes. The latter relationships have no clear interpretation. |
| `sun_MJ_m2_mean` | Strongly negatively correlated with precipitation (-0.82), `l_ed` (-0.43), min slope (-0.34), mean slope (-0.29), `prop_swf_within` (-0.25), and `l_shdi` (-0.21). | Strongly positively correlated with `temp_C_mean` (0.82), `l_ai` (0.43), `AFage` (0.34), area (0.29), and `treeage` (0.20). | The precipitation–temperature/radiation relationships are expected: cloudy conditions tend to coincide with rainfall and reduced solar radiation. The correlation with `l_ed` is less clear. As with temperature, sunnier fields tend to occur in more aggregated landscapes. Most remaining correlations are below 0.30 and should be relatively weak. |
| `precip_mm_sum` | Strongly negatively correlated with `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (-0.82), `temp_C_mean` (-0.77), `l_ai` (-0.65), area (-0.55), `treeage` (-0.40), and `l_contag` (-0.19). | Positively correlated with `l_ed` (0.65), min slope (0.55), mean slope (0.43), `prop_swf_within` (0.32), `l_shdi` (0.31), and clay (0.25). | Similar to the temperature and radiation patterns. However, precipitation shows overall stronger correlations with several landscape and field variables than the other climatic variables. |
| `clay` | Strongly negatively correlated with sand (-0.90), `temp_C_mean` (-0.46), `l_ai` (-0.42), and `prop_swf` (-0.21). | Positively correlated with silt (0.72), mean slope (0.58), `AFage` (0.47), `l_ed` (0.43), min slope (0.42), `l_shdi` (0.32), `l_contag` (0.32), precipitation (0.25), and max slope (0.24). | The silt–clay–sand correlations are expected because these are co-dependent components of soil texture. The slope relationship may indicate that clay-rich soils are more common in non-flat areas, potentially because clay contributes to soil structural stability. |
| `mean_slope` | Correlates negatively with `l_ai` (-0.66), sand (-0.64), area (-0.63), `treeage` (-0.52), `l_contag` (-0.49), `temp_C_mean` (-0.44), `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (-0.29), and `fert_N` (-0.18). | Very strongly correlated with min slope (0.89), `l_ed` (0.68), `l_shdi` (0.65), silt (0.60), clay (0.58), precipitation (0.43), max slope (0.37), `prop_swf` (0.20), and `prop_swf_within` (0.19). | As discussed for `l_shdi`, `l_ed`, and `temp_C_mean`, steeper fields are smaller, wetter/cooler, more clay/silt-rich, and occur in more fragmented landscapes. This suggests a coherent "steep upland field" cluster of correlated variables. |
| `min_slope` | NA | NA | Very similar to mean slope; better to keep only one of these variables. |
| `max_slope` | Correlates negatively with sand (-0.33), `l_ed` (-0.32), and `prop_swf_within` (-0.31). | Positively correlated with `l_shdi` (0.43), mean slope (0.37), `AFage` (0.37), `l_ai` (0.35), silt (0.35), `fert_N` (0.35), and clay (0.24). | Unlike mean and minimum slope, maximum slope appears to carry somewhat different information, most likely describing the steepest point within the field. |
| `prop_swf_within` | Correlates negatively with `l_shdi` (-0.59), `AFage` (-0.46), area (-0.42), `l_ai` (-0.41), max slope (-0.31), `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (-0.25), `l_contag` (-0.22), and `temp_C_mean` (-0.18). | Positively correlated with `prop_swf` (0.36), `l_ed` (0.36), min slope (0.35), precipitation (0.32), and mean slope (0.19). | The correlation with `AFage` is particularly interesting, suggesting that older fields tend to have fewer small woody features within the field. This could be confounded by tree harvesting or management history, which may also explain the lack of a similar relationship with `treeage`. |
| `fert_N` | Correlates negatively with `l_ed` (-0.46), min slope (-0.30), silt (-0.27), `prop_swf` (-0.19), and mean slope (-0.18). | Positively correlated with `l_ai` (0.45), max slope (0.35), `AFage` (0.25), and sand (0.23). | No clear interpretation. |
| `treeage` | Correlates negatively with mean slope (-0.52), min slope (-0.70), `l_ed` (-0.62), `l_shdi` (-0.46), `l_sidi` (-0.50), precipitation (-0.40), and `prop_swf` (-0.18). | Strongly positively correlated with area (0.77), `l_ai` (0.62), `l_contag` (0.52), `AFage` (0.35), `temp_C_mean` (0.22), and `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (0.20). | Older tree strips are found on larger, flatter, less fragmented, warmer/drier fields. There is no clear causal interpretation. This most plausibly reflects which regions or field types were selected for earlier agroforestry establishment rather than an effect of tree age itself. |
| `AFage` | Correlates negatively with `prop_swf_within` (-0.46), sand (-0.31), min slope (-0.29), `prop_swf` (-0.26), and `l_ed` (-0.23). | Positively correlated with `l_contag` (0.50), clay (0.47), area (0.42), max slope (0.37), `treeage` (0.35), `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (0.34), `l_ai` (0.25), `fert_N` (0.25), and `distance_to_tree_strip` (0.22). | The negative correlation with aggregation-related variables is interesting, although there is no clear interpretation. The soil-structure correlations are likely not causal, as `AFage` should not directly affect soil texture. |
| `area` | Correlates negatively with min slope (-0.82), `l_ed` (-0.65), mean slope (-0.63), precipitation (-0.55), `prop_swf_within` (-0.42), `l_shdi` (-0.41), and `prop_swf` (-0.34). | Strongly positively correlated with `treeage` (0.77), `l_contag` (0.74), `l_ai` (0.65), `AFage` (0.42), `sun_MJ_m2_mean` (0.29), and `temp_C_mean` (0.23). | Potentially confounded with field characteristics, as there is only one value per field. |
